questions.q:
Even the most wise don't / know what's hidden in / the depths of their being.

[SSC MTS Tier-01 16/06/23]
questions.s: The word "wise" needs to be in its superlative form, "wisest," for comparison of the highest degree.

questions.q:
Select the option that rectifies the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no correction is needed, select 'No correction required'.

Cinema provides the most universal entertainment.
questions.s:
The adjectives - empty, excellent, circular, extreme, chief, entire, complete, perfect, final, last, unique, universal, round, square, triangular, eternal, etc. are not used in the comparative or superlative degree.

So, using 'most' and 'more' before 'universal' is incorrect. So, the highlighted phrase requires replacement.

'Universal' starts with a vowel but is a consonant-sounding word. So, it shall be preceded by 'a', and not 'an'.

The correct sentence is: Cinema provides a universal entertainment.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

This almirah is made up of heavier metal.
questions.s:
heavier: Comparative, implies comparison not present in the sentence.

heaviest: Superlative, for more than two items.

most heavier: Incorrect grammar.

most heaviest: Incorrect grammar.

heavy: Base adjective, fits a simple description.

Correct sentence: "This almirah is made up of heavy metal."

questions.q: He was not able to give many time to his research.
questions.s: Explanation:- (a) use ‘much’ instead of ‘many’ kyunki time ek uncountable noun hai iske sath 'many' ka use nahi kiya jaa sakta isliye 'much' ka use hoga.

questions.q: Radha climbed the / ladder cautious, / but she fell off / despite being careful.
questions.s:
Cautious” is an adjective, but here it is incorrectly used to describe how Radha climbed.
The sentence needs a describing word that correctly fits the action, and “cautious” cannot function in that position.
Correct form: Radha climbed the ladder cautiously…

questions.q: Until few decades ago, / researchers believed the moon / was completely dry. (SSC MTS Tier-01 17/05/23)
questions.s: 'Few' implies a negative (almost none). 'A few' implies a small, positive number.

questions.q: His performance was funnier than her.
questions.s:
The sentence contains an error. The correct pronoun to use after "than" should be in the objective case, "than her" is incorrect; it should be "than hers."

The corrected sentence would be: “His performance was funnier than hers.”

questions.q: No less than thousands of spectators are/ waiting for Dhoni to come out/ in the field and play his / masterful stroke.
o: No less than thousands of spectators are
questions.s: Explanation:- Use fewer in place of less. Kyunki 'no less than' is phrase ka use uncountable cheezon ke liye hota hai aur 'no fewer than' is phrase ka use countable cheezon ke liye hota hai. Aage likha thousands of spectators se pata chal rha hai ki veh countable hai plural hai isliye 'no fewer than' ka use hoga.

questions.q: He found (a wooden broken chair) in the room,
o: broken and wooden chair
questions.s:
Adjective order rule: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose + Noun
Condition comes before material, so the correct order is: a broken wooden chair

questions.q: My All students passed the exam with flying colors.
questions.s:
" Possessive case comes after ‘All’ and ‘Both’ and not before them. The correct option is (c) "My All students.

The corrected sentence should be: "All my students passed the exam with flying colors."

questions.q: Your body will respond by / getting more muscular and/ strong before you know it. (SSC MTS Tier-01 13/06/23)
questions.s: For parallelism, 'strong' should be in its comparative form 'stronger' to match 'more muscular'.

questions.q: All these boys have come to college without few knowledge of English.
questions.s: Explanation:- (a) Use ‘any’ instead of ‘few’ kyunki knowledge noun uncountable hota hai aur 'few' countable ke liye lagta hai isliye few toh aa nahi sakta dusri baat yahan par 'little' bhi nahi aa sakta kyunki 'without' laga hone ki wajah se sentence ka meaning already negative ho chuka hai. Yahan par ek neutral word lagana padega jo na positive ho na hi negative ho isliye meaning ke according yahan 'any' word ka use kiya jayega.
